questions.question: Which of the following tribes does NOT live in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maasai**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Maasai** is a tribe that predominantly lives in **Kenya and Tanzania**.
 
• They are known for their distinct culture, customs, and dress.
 
• Unlike the other tribes listed in the question (Gond, Santhal, Tharu), the Maasai do not have a presence in India.
 
• The Maasai people are semi-nomadic and are known for their traditional lifestyle and resistance to modern cultural influences.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gond** is one of the largest tribal groups in India, found mainly in **Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Odisha, and Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• **Santhal** is a prominent tribe in India, primarily residing in **Jharkhand, West Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha**.
 
• **Tharu** is a tribal community living in the Terai region of **Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, and Bihar **in India.
 
• These tribes (Gond, Santhal, Tharu) contribute to India's rich cultural and ethnic diversity.

questions.question: Who was the first to use the term 'horsepower' that refers to the power produced by an engine?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**James Watt**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **James Watt** was the first to use the term '**horsepower**' to quantify the power produced by an engine.
 
• He coined the term in the late 18th century as a way to help market his improved steam engine.
 
• Watt's definition of horsepower was based on the **amount of work a horse could do over a certain period**.
 
• This unit of measurement became widely adopted and is still used today to describe the power output of engines.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **James Watt** was a Scottish inventor, mechanical engineer, and chemist who made significant improvements to the **Newcomen steam engine**.
 
• His enhancements to the steam engine played a key role in the Industrial Revolution by making it more efficient and powerful.
 
• **The watt, a unit of power **in the International System of Units, is named in his honor.
 
• Watt's contributions to engineering and energy measurement have had a lasting impact on technology and industry.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an alignment option for text in a cell?

__
 
• **Justified** is not an alignment option for text in a cell in most spreadsheet applications.
 
• Common text alignment options in spreadsheet applications include **Left, Center, and Right** alignments.
 
• Text alignment determines how the text is positioned within the cell.
 
• Proper text alignment enhances the readability and organization of data in a spreadsheet.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Left alignment** aligns the text to the left side of the cell.
 
• **Center alignment** centers the text horizontally within the cell.
 
• **Right alignment** aligns the text to the right side of the cell.
 
• Some spreadsheet applications may offer additional alignment options, such as **Top, Middle, and Bottom** vertical alignments.

questions.question: _______ is one of the well-known schemes sponsored by the Union Government of India. It was launched in November 2015 with the aim of rescuing the country’s ailing electricity distribution companies.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ujwal DISCOM Assurance Yojana**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ujwal DISCOM Assurance Yojana (UDAY)** is one of the well-known schemes sponsored by the Union Government of India.
 
• It was launched in **November 2015** with the aim of rescuing the country's ailing electricity distribution companies.
 
• The scheme focuses on improving the operational and financial efficiency of DISCOMs (Distribution Companies).
 
• Under UDAY, states take over 75% of the DISCOM debt, thereby reducing the interest burden and improving financial stability.
 
• The scheme also emphasizes on reducing AT&C (Aggregate Technical and Commercial) losses, improving billing and collection efficiency, and promoting energy efficiency measures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The other options listed in the question pertain to various other initiatives and schemes related to the power sector in India.
 
• **One Nation, One Grid** aims at providing a single grid for electricity transmission across the country.
 
• **Integrated Power Development Scheme (IPDS)** focuses on strengthening sub-transmission and distribution networks in urban areas.
 
• **Deendayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana** aims at rural electrification and feeder separation to improve the supply of electricity in rural areas.

questions.question: Which of the following committees had recommended the inclusion of a chapter on the Fundamental Duties in the Constitution of India and stressed that the citizens should become conscious that, in addition to the enjoyment of rights, they also have certain duties to perform?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Swaran Singh Committee (1976)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Swaran Singh Committee** was appointed by the government in 1976 to make recommendations on the Constitution, which included the incorporation of Fundamental Duties.
 
• Following the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee, the **42nd Amendment Act** of **1976 **added a new chapter, **Part IVA**, to the Constitution, which enumerates the Fundamental Duties of citizens.
 
• The idea behind the inclusion of Fundamental Duties was to remind citizens that they have certain responsibilities towards the nation, in addition to enjoying their rights.
 
• There are currently **11 Fundamental Duties** listed in **Article 51A** of the Constitution of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **42nd Amendment Act** is also known as the "**Mini-Constitution**" due to the extensive changes it made to the Constitution.
 
• The concept of Fundamental Duties was borrowed from the Constitution of the former Soviet Union.
 
• Fundamental Duties are **non-justiciable**, meaning they are not enforceable by the courts for their violation.
 
• The inclusion of Fundamental Duties aims to promote a sense of discipline and commitment among citizens towards the nation.
 
• Some of the duties include respecting the national symbols, cherishing the heritage of the country, and protecting the environment.

questions.question: Which of the following persons was sworn in as chief of the Central Information Commission of India in November 2023?

__
 
• **Heeralal Samariya** was sworn in as the chief of the **Central Information Commission** of India in** November 2023**.
 
• The Central Information Commission is an important body **set up under the Right to Information Act (RTI)** to act upon complaints from those who have been unable to submit their requests for information to a Central Public Information Officer or State Public Information Officer.
 
• The commission plays a crucial role in ensuring transparency and accountability in the functioning of public authorities.
 
• Heeralal Samariya has previously held various significant positions in the government, contributing to his extensive experience in administration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Central Information Commission was constituted with effect from **12th October 2005 under the RTI Act, 2005**.
 
• The Chief Information Commissioner and Information Commissioners are **appointed by the President of India **on the recommendation of a committee consisting of the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister.
 
• The **tenure **of the Chief Information Commissioner is typically up to **5 years or until they attain the age of 65 years**, whichever is earlier.
 
• The commission has been instrumental in promoting transparency and accountability in the working of the public authorities and has handled numerous significant cases regarding the right to information.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a moon of Jupiter?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Triton**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Triton** is not a moon of Jupiter.
 
• **Callisto**, **Ganymede**, and **Europa** are all moons of Jupiter.
 
• **Triton** is actually the largest moon of Neptune.
 
• Jupiter has numerous moons, with the four largest being the Galilean moons: **Io, Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto**.
 
• These moons were first observed by Galileo Galilei in 1610 and are some of the largest objects in our Solar System outside the Sun and the eight planets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jupiter** is the largest planet in our Solar System and has a very strong magnetic field.
 
• Jupiter's atmosphere is primarily composed of hydrogen and helium, with traces of other gases.
 
• Jupiter's Great Red Spot is a giant storm that has been raging for hundreds of years.
 
• Jupiter's moons are of great interest to scientists because some of them, like Europa, may have subsurface oceans that could potentially harbor life.
 
• Neptune's moon **Triton** is unique because it has a retrograde orbit, meaning it orbits in the opposite direction to Neptune's rotation.

questions.question: National income at constant prices means:

options.text: income estimated at base year prices
income estimated at any year prices
income estimated for next year prices
income estimated at current year prices

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**income estimated at base year prices**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Income estimated at base year prices** refers to national income calculated using the prices of a specific base year, which helps in eliminating the effects of inflation and provides a more accurate measure of real income over different periods.
 
• This method allows for a consistent comparison of economic performance over time by adjusting for changes in price levels.
 
• It is also known as** national income at constant prices or real national income**.
 
• Using base year prices helps in understanding the actual growth of the economy without the distortion caused by fluctuating prices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The concept of national income at constant prices is crucial for economic analysis and policy-making.
 
• It helps in understanding the real growth of different sectors of the economy.
 
• The base year is periodically updated to reflect more recent economic conditions and to provide a more accurate measure of real economic performance.
 
• National income is a vital indicator of the economic health of a country and is used for planning and development purposes.
 
• Organizations like the** Central Statistical Office (CSO)** in India are responsible for calculating and publishing national income data.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most dominant species of the Tropical Deciduous Forests?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Teak**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Teak** is the most dominant species of the Tropical Deciduous Forests.
 
• Tropical Deciduous Forests, also known as Monsoon Forests, are characterized by trees that shed their leaves annually during the dry season.
 
• These forests are found in areas with a distinct dry and wet season, primarily in parts of India, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America.
 
• Teak trees are valued for their high-quality wood, which is durable, water-resistant, and used extensively in furniture making, shipbuilding, and other applications.
 
• The presence of teak in these forests contributes significantly to the local economy and biodiversity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tropical Deciduous Forests** are divided into two types: Moist Deciduous and Dry Deciduous.
 
• **Moist Deciduous Forests** are found in regions with moderate rainfall and include species like teak, sal, and shisham.
 
• **Dry Deciduous Forests** occur in areas with lower rainfall and include species like acacia, thorn, and euphorbia.
 
• These forests play a crucial role in maintaining ecological balance, supporting wildlife, and providing resources for human use.
 
• Conservation efforts are essential to protect these forests from deforestation and degradation.

questions.question: The birthday of _______ is celebrated as the International Day of Non-Violence.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahatma Gandhi**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The birthday of **Mahatma Gandhi** is celebrated as the **International Day of Non-Violence**.
 
• This day is observed on **2nd October** each year, commemorating Gandhi's birth anniversary.
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi** is renowned globally for his philosophy of non-violence (Ahimsa) and his role in leading India to independence through peaceful means.
 
• The United Nations General Assembly established this day in 2007 to disseminate the message of non-violence through education and public awareness.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahatma Gandhi**, also known as the Father of the Nation in India, was born on **2nd October 1869** in Porbandar, Gujarat.
 
• His full name was **Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi**.
 
• He led various significant movements such as the **Non-Cooperation Movement**, the **Civil Disobedience Movement**, and the **Quit India Movement** against British rule in India.
 
• Gandhi's principles of non-violence and civil disobedience have inspired many global leaders and movements for civil rights and freedom across the world.
 
• 2nd October is also celebrated as **Gandhi Jayanti** in India, a national holiday in his honor.

questions.question: Under the discretionary power of which Article of the Indian Constitution did the SC of India recognise sex work as a profession?

• It was under this discretionary power that the** Supreme Court of India recognized sex work as a profession**.
 
• The recognition aims to protect the rights and dignity of sex workers and to ensure their safety and well-being.

• The article empowers the Supreme Court to ensure that its orders are implemented and justice is achieved, even if it means going beyond the existing legal framework.
 
• This provision underscores the role of the judiciary in upholding the principles of justice and the rule of law in India.

• Once the textbox is created, you can type your desired text into it.
 
• You can also format the text using various formatting options available in the **Home** tab.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Textboxes can be resized by clicking and dragging the handles on the edges of the textbox.
 
• You can move the textbox to a different location on the slide by clicking and dragging it.
 
• Textboxes can also be used to add titles, subtitles, or any other text-based information to your slides.
 
• In addition to textboxes, you can also add other elements like shapes, images, and charts to enhance your presentation.
 
• MS-PowerPoint offers various design and animation options to make your text and other elements more visually appealing.

questions.question: Which part of the Constitution of India deals with ‘Citizenship’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Part II**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Part II** of the Constitution of India deals with the provisions related to **Citizenship**.
 
• This part includes **Articles 5 to 11**, which lay down the laws concerning who may be regarded as a citizen of India.
 
• It covers various aspects such as citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution, rights of citizenship of certain persons who have migrated from Pakistan, and other provisions related to the acquisition and termination of citizenship.
 
• Citizenship is a crucial aspect as it determines the rights and duties of individuals within the Indian state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written** constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Seventh Schedule** of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the **Union, State, and Concurrent lists**.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.
 
• The Union List has been amended several times to meet the evolving needs of the nation.
